title: Next free order numbers
prompt:
used lists order numbers that are already taken, in any order. It may contain repeats, zero, negative numbers and very large numbers. Return the k smallest positive integers that are not in used, from smallest to largest.

- used has 0 to 100,000 integers between -10^9 and 10^9.
- k is between 1 and 100,000.
- Target O(n + k) time. You may rearrange used in place.
hints: With n values, only numbers 1 to n can fill the first n slots. Place each such value v at index v − 1 with cyclic sort and skip the rest.
Scan the slots: index j that does not hold j + 1 means j + 1 is free. Stop once you have k answers.
If you still need more after the scan, keep counting from n + 1 upwards, but skip any value larger than n that was in used. Remember those in a set during the scan.

solution.explanation: Cyclic sort places every value 1..n at its home index; values outside that range, and repeats, are left in the gaps. A scan lists the free numbers up to n in order. Values above n sit only in gaps, so collecting them during the scan gives a small set to skip while counting upwards from n + 1. At most n of those candidates are skipped, so the second loop runs at most k + n times.

complexity.notes: Placement and the scan are O(n). The set holds only values above n that sit in gaps, at most n of them. Without rearranging, a hash set of used gives the same time with O(n) space as well.

followUps: used is already sorted. Find the k-th free number in O(log n) with binary search.
Numbers are allocated and released over time. Design a structure that always hands out the smallest free number.
